findings.finding: The plan asserts 'infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json hard-codes the five doomed check names' and lists updating it as in-scope. Reading the actual snapshot reveals it contains `clean core wheel (no extras → heavy deps absent)` as a required status check — a name the plan says is being KEPT byte-identical. If the new single job produces a different job name (e.g. 'venv-loop (per-extra + union)' instead of individual per-extra names), the snapshot's `clean core wheel` entry must be preserved. However, the snapshot also lacks `mcp` and `grounding` check names entirely (they were in the matrix but never in the protection snapshot), meaning a rollback would NOT require those checks — an asymmetry the plan does not mention. The count 'five doomed check names' is also off: the snapshot has import-linter + agents + eval + tracing + union = 5 removed, but the plan implies the new collapsed job will produce a single new check name that isn't in the snapshot at all — meaning the rollback protection would have NO entry for the new job.
scenarios: After the plan executes, rollback via rollback-mirror-lock.sh would recreate a ruleset requiring 'extra "agents" installs' et al. — checks that can no longer exist — freezing the ability to merge to main post-rollback.

findings.finding: The checked-in guard that 'asserts the two optionality test files collect 9 items' hardcodes a count (9) that is expected to evolve as contributors add tests to those files, yet the plan provides no maintenance story for updating the count and does not make it configurable. When a new test is added, this guard will turn red with no obvious fix, or will be silently bumped to an arbitrary number, defeating its purpose as a coverage floor.
findings.location: Testing section, paragraph 1; Acceptance Criteria line 7
scenarios: A contributor adds a tenth test to test_core_optionality.py; CI goes red on test_ci_workflow_parity.py; confused by a failing 'parity' test, they bump 9→10 without understanding the intent, which is now just an exact-count assertion rather than a floor
The count is silently lowered to match after a test is deleted, destroying the floor guarantee the plan was designed to provide
findings.suggested_fix: In the test: `assert collected_count >= 9, f'Expected at least 9 optionality tests; got {collected_count}. Do not lower this floor.'`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-count-9 assertion (AC item 7) with an assertion on the specific test node IDs (e.g., `pytest --collect-only -q` output contains each of the 9 named test functions), so the guard catches removal or re-marking of the specific repaid tests rather than snapshotting a count.
evidence: "assert `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` and `tests/unit/test_optional.py` are collected under `-m "not integration and not external"` and yield 9 items (repays the deleted job)"
ABSENCE: no assertion on specific test node IDs; count-only assertion cannot detect test replacement
findings.finding: The checked-in test for collection count (AC item 7) hardcodes the exact number 9. When new tests are legitimately added to `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` or `tests/unit/test_optional.py`, the assertion will fail and a developer will bump the number to fix CI — silently re-validating collection — but over time this becomes a pure change-detector that snapshots the current count rather than asserting the behavioral contract ('these specific test IDs are collected'). More critically, it provides no guard against individual tests being removed: 9→9 with one test deleted and one added still passes. The real invariant is identity of the specific test node IDs, not their count.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC item 7 / Testing section paragraph 1
scenarios: A developer adds a new optionality test → CI guard breaks on count mismatch, developer bumps to 10, guard is now a no-op change-detector
A developer renames one of the 9 tests (e.g. adding an `@pytest.mark.integration` marker removes it from count) and adds a new unrelated test → count stays 9, guard passes, repayment is silently lost
findings.suggested_fix: In the new `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` guard, collect via `pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py tests/unit/test_optional.py -m 'not integration and not external'` and assert the result contains each of the 9 specific test function names (e.g., `test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack`, etc.) rather than asserting `len(items) == 9`. This is immune to both count-bumping and silent substitution.
